Notes: First documentary mention: interdict of Bishop Giraldo (1215) on gambling between Jews and Christians; a Roman-era/Council of Elvira presence is claimed but not documented
Bishop Giraldo's 1215 interdict censuring bets between Jews and Christians of San Miguel parish; Jews living in the city centre
'The first references to Jewish settlement in Segovia are from the 13th century' (century midpoint used)
About four decades after 1215 a new norm speaks of 'an important community' (year approximate)
A Jewish butcher shop (carnicería judía) documented in 1287

Estimate based on families: kabbalist Jacob ha-Cohen spoke of 'the community of 65 families that prayed there more than a hundred years' earlier; source dates him to late 14th c. (other sources c.1280) so date is uncertain, taken as late 13th c.
Considerable community paid 10806 maravedis in taxes in 1294 (tax figure, not population)
'At the end of this century [13th] there were around 300 Jews in Segovia' (year 1300 used for end of century)
Jews failed to pay the 30 dineros each Jew aged 14+ owed the bishop
Archbishop of Toledo condemned joint fasting of Jewish and Christian women in Segovia
Estimate based on families: 'the Jewish community had between 50 and 100 families' in the 14th century (range ~250-500; midpoint; century midpoint used as year)
'Synagogue of Burgos' in San Miguel parish documented 1358
Old main synagogue used as a synagogue from c.1373 until 1410; converted into a church 1419
Sinagoga Mayor first documented in 1373; historian Yolanda Moreno Koch documents seven synagogues
Estimate based on families: 'In about 1390 there were about 50 Jewish homeowners in Segovia. There were 23 craftsmen' (homeowners x5)
Persecutions of 1391: authorities unable to protect the Jews; some converted
Host desecration charge; two distinguished Jews executed incl. Meir Alguades the king's physician
Main synagogue transformed into Corpus Christi church (16 Oct 1412); smaller synagogue given to a monastery 12 Apr 1413; Laws of Ayllon segregation
Jews of Segovia accused of profaning the host (date per this source)
Sinagoga del Campo erected in 1456
Taxes of the aljama amounted to 11000 maravedis; massacre of Marranos (conversos) on 16 May 1474
First document of the New Main Synagogue dates from 1476; Abraham Seneor named Rab Mayor of Castilian Jewry 1476
From 1481 Jews confined to an enclosed Juderia with seven gates; 'the population of the Jewish quarter multiplied by four' after confinement
Between 1464 and 1482 Segovia's aljama contributed the most in taxes of all Castilian aljamas; Inquisition established 1486
'At that time the community of Segovia was the most important one in Castile'; expulsion decree May 1492; exiles probably left for Portugal
Expulsion: Jews fled to caves near the cemetery when the deadline expired; many died there, others were baptized
'After the Expulsion Edict in 1492 the Segovian aljama disappears' (remaining Jews converted; conversos not counted)
